name: Count The Blocks
description: You wrote down all integers from $$$0$$$ to $$$10^n - 1$$$, padding them with leading zeroes so their lengths are exactly $$$n$$$. For example, if $$$n = 3$$$ then you wrote out 000 , 001 , ..., 998 , 999 . A block in an integer $$$x$$$ is a consecutive segment of equal digits that cannot be extended to the left or to the right. For example, in the integer $$$00027734000$$$ there are three blocks of length $$$1$$$, one block of length $$$2$$$ and two blocks of length $$$3$$$. For all integers $$$i$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ count the number of blocks of length $$$i$$$ among the written down integers. Since these integers may be too large, print them modulo $$$998244353$$$.
input_specification: The only line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$).
output_specification: In the only line print $$$n$$$ integers. The $$$i$$$-th integer is equal to the number of blocks of length $$$i$$$. Since these integers may be too large, print them modulo $$$998244353$$$.
approach_summary: Express count as f(R) - f(L-1). Define memoized state dp[pos][tight][leading_zeros][cond] scanning digits from most to least significant in O(digits × base × states).
